subject: general
question: Which of the following temples of India is called the Great Living Chola Temple?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brihadisvara temple in Thanjavur**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Brihadisvara temple in Thanjavur** is recognized as the Great Living Chola Temple.
 
• This temple is a part of the **UNESCO World Heritage Site** known as the "Great Living Chola Temples" which includes the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur, the Brihadisvara Temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram, and the Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram.
 
• The Brihadisvara temple was built by the Chola emperor **Raja Raja Chola I** between 1003 and 1010 AD.
 
• It is a magnificent example of Chola architecture, showcasing the advanced techniques and grandeur of the Chola dynasty.
 
• The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is renowned for its massive tower (vimana), intricate sculptures, and expansive courtyards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Chola dynasty** was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in the history of southern India, known for its contributions to art, architecture, and culture.
 
• The Chola temples are characterized by their grand scale, intricate carvings, and use of granite.
 
• The Brihadisvara temple is also known as **Rajarajeswaram** and Peruvudaiyar Kovil.
 
• The temple's central tower, or Vimana, is one of the tallest of its kind in the world, standing at about 66 meters (216 feet).
 
• The temple complex includes shrines for various deities, a massive statue of Nandi (the bull), and numerous other sculptures and frescoes depicting various aspects of Hindu mythology.
